What to look for: the ray payload size the issue asks for is already in the
compiler's own output, in the dx.entryPoints named metadata at the bottom of
the DXIL pane. Each entry there is a list of tag/value pairs. Tag 8 is the
shader kind (7 raygeneration, 8 intersection, 9 anyhit, 10 closesthit,
11 miss, 12 callable), tag 6 is the ray payload size in bytes, and tag 7 is
the intersection attribute size in bytes. This shader declares a 28-byte
payload, an 8-byte attribute struct and a 12-byte callable parameter, so the
anyhit and closesthit entries carry 28 and 8, the miss entry carries 28, and
the callable entry carries 12. The raygeneration and intersection entries
carry neither, because neither takes a payload. The same three values are
also written into the container's RDAT part as PayloadSizeInBytes,
AttributeSizeInBytes and ShaderKind.

What Compiler Explorer cannot show is the actual subject of the issue. There
is no way to call a reflection interface from here, so the finding that
ID3D12FunctionReflection exposes the shader kind but has no field that can
hold the payload size comes from a purpose-built harness recorded in the
triage notes, not from this pane. Treat this link as evidence that the data
exists and has existed in every tested stable release, not as evidence about
the API.

Both panes are expected to compile cleanly and to agree. That is the point:
this is a feature request about API surface, not a bug, and nothing here
changed between the oldest compiler Compiler Explorer offers and trunk.
